item.title: Claude and ChatGPT Finance Tools Compare Privacy and Features
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Claude Personal Finance vs. ChatGPT Finances: What sets them apart?
Anthropic's Claude Personal Finance and OpenAI's ChatGPT Finances both analyze user bank accounts via Plaid partnerships, offering read-only access to balances, transactions, and financial data. Both tools generate visual dashboards for expenses and savings. Privacy settings differ: Claude's data from Personal Finance isn't used to train models by default, and unlinked accounts erase data immediately. ChatGPT requires users to opt out of data sharing via settings, with synced data deleted within 30 days after disconnection. Claude excludes ads and financial products, while OpenAI tests ads for cheaper tiers. OpenAI plans to expand Finances with Intuit for credit cards and taxes, while Anthropic seeks feedback from financial institutions to improve Personal Finance. Both tools avoid offering expert advice but provide general financial guidance.

item.title: Tech Enthusiast Retires 27-Year Microsoft Exchange Server
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Enthusiast abandons self-hosted Microsoft Exchange after 27 years, moving mailboxes to Microsoft 365
A homelab enthusiast has retired their 27-year-old Microsoft Exchange server, replacing it with Postfix on Ubuntu Server LTS. The user, Meta4X, moved mailboxes to Microsoft 365 years ago but kept Exchange running as a relay for local network alerts. After Microsoft ended support for Exchange 2019 and shifted to a subscription model, Meta4X decided to retire the server, citing accumulated technical debt. The setup began with Exchange 5.5 on Windows NT 4, evolving through multiple versions up to 2019. Meta4X noted that existing Exchange 2019 licenses could technically be used with Exchange SE under certain arrangements, but they opted to retire the system regardless. The migration to Postfix includes implementing STARTTLS, Let’s Encrypt certificates, and boot encryption. Commentators noted other alternatives like Mailcow and Grommunio, while acknowledging that Postfix’s security still requires careful configuration. The move ends a long-running on-premises email setup, with Meta4X emphasizing the need to address aging infrastructure.

item.title: Spammers obtain numbers via data breaches, illegal calls, and phishing
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: How do spam callers get your number in the first place?
Spammers obtain phone numbers through data breaches, illegal calls, and third-party data sales. Numbers may be acquired via random robocalls, stolen from public records like court filings, or purchased from data brokers who legally resell contact information after users sign up for services. Phishing scams also expose numbers when victims fill out fake login pages or sign up for fraudulent websites. The FTC's Do Not Call Registry limits telemarketing calls but does not block charities, political groups, or debt collectors. Users can check if their numbers were part of a data breach by searching their email on sites like Have I Been Pwned. Protecting personal information involves avoiding suspicious websites, hiding numbers on public profiles, and limiting account creation. Robocallers may still contact users even with precautions, but registry enrollment and vigilance reduce risk.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Router overheating can cause connectivity issues and damage
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Is your router overheating? Here's how to keep it cool and working safely
Home routers generate heat during operation, but excessive temperatures can cause connectivity issues or hardware damage. Modern routers use system-on-a-chip (SoC) designs, such as Broadcom's BCM6765, which integrate networking components. Overheating may result from poor ventilation, faulty power adapters, or aging hardware. Symptoms include tactile heat, intermittent connectivity, speed drops, and Wi-Fi range loss. Solutions include ensuring proper airflow by avoiding enclosed spaces and direct sunlight, cleaning vents to prevent dust buildup, and updating firmware for stability improvements. If these steps fail, a faulty power adapter may be the cause, requiring replacement. If all else fails, the router itself may be failing and require replacement. Proper ventilation and maintenance can prevent overheating and extend router lifespan.

item.title: Ericsson's Drone Tracking Tech Uses Mobile Networks to Detect UAVs
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Drones can now be tracked down by mobile networks alone — could this new Ericsson tech spell the end for the current crop of flying UAVs?
Ericsson is developing technology to detect and track drones using existing mobile networks instead of dedicated surveillance systems. Its Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) system analyzes radio signals bouncing off flying objects, leveraging cellular infrastructure to identify drone movements. Trials by AT&T in Texas and Finland's Erillisverkot confirmed the system's ability to detect and follow drones using signal reflections. The technology requires specialized equipment like Massive MIMO antennas and software, rather than functioning on all existing networks. Ericsson aims to start limited commercial trials in 2027. The system could address security threats from unauthorized drones disrupting airports and military sites, as seen in Jersey Airport incidents. Ian Fogg of CCS Insight noted mobile networks' advantage in detecting low-flying drones compared to radar, with 6G's new spectrum improving detection accuracy. While the tech could also monitor shipping and weather, it is intended to complement, not replace, existing radar systems. Challenges include ensuring accuracy in complex environments with buildings and competing signals.

item.title: Bluetooth HDT Enables Lossless Audio for Audiophiles
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: New Bluetooth High Data Throughput may finally satisfy audiophiles
Bluetooth SIG announced High Data Throughput (HDT) on November 4, offering up to 7.5 Mbps bandwidth, four times that of Bluetooth LE 2M. This feature targets high-bandwidth applications like AI, spatial computing, and lossless audio, potentially satisfying audiophiles who have long criticized Bluetooth for lacking sufficient bandwidth for uncompressed audio. Previous Bluetooth versions, including LE 2M, could not reliably transmit CD-quality lossless audio due to compression limitations. HDT provides higher bandwidth, improved reliability, and lower power usage, enabling transmission of 24-bit 48 kHz audio (2.3 Mbps) and even 24-bit 96 kHz (4.6 Mbps), though 24-bit 192 kHz (9.2 Mbps) exceeds the maximum. While HDT compliance requires specific versions (HDT2-HDT4), the highest 7.5 Mbps is optional. Device tuning remains critical for optimal performance, but HDT could enable wireless alternatives to wired audiophile equipment.

item.title: Overcharging Smartwatches Accelerates Battery Degradation
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: You’re overcharging your smartwatch, and it’s aging the battery
Overcharging smartwatches accelerates battery degradation. Lithium-ion batteries in smartwatches lose capacity over time due to charging cycles and prolonged full charges. Leaving a watch at 100% for hours stresses the battery, even with built-in overcharge prevention. Modern models like the Apple Watch Series 11, Google Pixel Watch 5, and Samsung Galaxy Watch9 now last up to 40 hours with AOD enabled, reducing the need for overnight charging. Shorter top-ups during daily activities are sufficient. However, replacing smartwatch batteries is difficult due to sealed designs and glued components, often costing around $100. Users should avoid full charges and keep battery levels between 20–80% to prolong lifespan. Proper care could extend a smartwatch's battery life through multiple smartphone upgrades.

item.title: Tom's Hardware Premium Highlights Tech Developments in November 2026
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: This week in Tom's Hardware Premium: November 7, 2026
Tom's Hardware Premium highlights key tech developments for November 7, 2026. Apple's decision to release a PROLED display with touch in 2026 is analyzed, despite similar features existing in Windows laptops. Micron's product roadmap includes 1δ DRAM manufactured in the U.S. and 11th-Gen NAND with over 400 layers. ASML's FDX Fusion technology uses DUV instead of EUV for 7nm-class performance, per GlobalFoundries VP Sudipto Bose. A PHP vulnerability analysis examines cybersecurity risks from outdated software. Google's Gemini 4 Carbon model is evaluated as a top AI contender with lower hallucination risks. Nagare Labs' Z2RAM, a potential alternative to HBF, is in early testing. Subscription access to detailed articles and Bench benchmarking database is promoted.

item.title: Windows 11 Beta Adds Redesigned Search, Enhanced Facial Recognition
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Windows 11 is getting redesigned Search and improved facial recognition in its latest beta
Microsoft is rolling out updates to Windows 11 through its latest Insider Beta Build 26320.9876, released November 6. The update includes a redesigned Search interface using WinUI 3, offering faster results and better navigation. Users can now perform actions like enabling Bluetooth, switching to dark mode, adjusting brightness, muting audio, and arranging windows via Search. The feature also improves typo and synonym recognition. Windows Hello now temporarily brightens the screen during facial recognition, and Live captions can capture microphone audio, system sounds, or both. Quick settings for Xbox mode allow gamers to access system controls without leaving the interface. Microsoft notes the version change to 26H2 doesn’t include major new features. No release date was provided for these Insider features to reach regular Windows 11 users.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Fitbit users should restart device for specific issues
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: How often should you restart your Fitbit watch?
Fitbit users should restart their devices for specific issues. Restarting can resolve problems like failed app sync, unresponsive screens, or delayed data tracking. The process varies by model: newer devices require navigating settings menus, while older models use physical buttons or charging cables. Users should avoid inserting objects into sensor holes. Restarting is a simple troubleshooting step, but frequent use isn't recommended unless needed. If issues persist, a device upgrade may be necessary. Instructions include holding buttons for 10 seconds or using charging cables for screenless models. The process preserves data unlike a reset, which deletes information. Restarting can also fix unresponsive devices or reboot loops caused by environmental factors like saltwater exposure.

item.title: How long should a PC processor actually last?
item.description:
Source: Engadget
PC processors typically last a decade or more with proper care, though they may become obsolete rather than fail from wear. Manufacturers don't specify lifespans, but regular use doesn't degrade CPUs. Common failure signs include random freezes, boot issues, or restarts, often linked to other hardware. Overheating is a major stressor, with temperatures above 60°C under load or 80°C during intensive tasks indicating potential cooling issues. Users should monitor CPU usage via Task Manager, ensuring it stays below 20% under normal conditions. Overclocking can reduce lifespan but may still allow use until obsolescence. Power surges or faulty power supplies pose greater risks than age-related failure. Regular cleaning, adequate airflow, and thermal paste maintenance improve longevity. CPUs are more likely to be replaced due to performance limitations than mechanical failure, especially if cooled properly and maintained.

item.title: TSMC Denies 3D DRAM Production for Nvidia, Cites Focus on Logic Foundry
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: TSMC denies exploring 3D DRAM at Nvidia's request
TSMC denies exploring 3D DRAM production at Nvidia's request, stating it remains focused on logic foundry operations. A report from The Information suggested TSMC is preparing plans for 3D DRAM manufacturing following Nvidia's request, but TSMC spokespersons emphasized their commitment to core IC foundry business. Two insiders confirmed TSMC is developing 3D DRAM plans, led by Hsu Kuo-chin, vice president of advanced packaging. The initiative comes amid global memory shortages that have elevated DRAM to a strategic asset. TSMC lacks DRAM manufacturing expertise and capacity, with 3D DRAM production requiring entirely new fabrication techniques. Major DRAM makers like Micron, Samsung, and SK hynix are also pursuing 3D DRAM, though Micron plans to prioritize planar DRAM technologies for years. TSMC would need to invest billions in R&D to develop competitive DRAM processes, facing risks like market oversupply and antitrust scrutiny. Alternatives include partnering with DRAM manufacturers or focusing on logic base dies for HBM. TSMC could expand its role in advanced memory without direct DRAM production by integrating memory with processors via SoIC technology.

item.title: iOS Blocks Autocomplete for 4,500+ Phrases, Study Reveals
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: iOS Apparently Maintains a List of 4,500+ Phrases It Won’t Autocomplete
iOS maintains a list of over 4,500 phrases it refuses to autocomplete, according to researcher Derik Kauffman. The list, dubbed a 'gray list,' includes slurs, insults, and politically sensitive terms like 'Tibetan independence' and 'Kashmir dispute.' Apple avoids offering potentially offensive suggestions but does not explain specific exclusions. The list blocks phrases such as 'son of a bitch' and 'crystal meth,' while allowing some variations like 'bad boy' but not 'bad girl.' Notably, 'Trayvon Martin' is on the list, as are phrases like 'make America great again' and 'Covid was a hoax.' Swipe typing sometimes bypasses these restrictions, but typed words are blocked. Apple told Reuters its keyboard avoids inappropriate suggestions but users can override predictions. The list includes language-specific terms like 'العدوان الإسرائيلي' and '台独.' Kauffman published the findings on Swipeblocked, warning the list contains explicit content.

item.title: Binance CFO Departs After $6.3 Billion Hack, Company Covers Losses
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch, Gizmodo Original headline: Binance CFO Departs Following $6.3 Billion Hack, Company Commits to Covering Losses
Binance’s chief financial officer, Kaiser Ng, has left the cryptocurrency exchange following a $6.3 billion hack. Co-CEO Yi He cited Ng’s departure as enabling a new venture, with a six-month transition plan. Ng will be replaced by Justin Yek. The hack, attributed to North Korean group TraderTraitor, prompted a $3.6 billion user withdrawal after Binance unfroze accounts. The company claims it absorbed all losses using reserves, with $2.85 billion in stolen assets intercepted and $3.3 billion deemed irrecoverable. The FBI and TRM Labs point to TraderTraitor as the perpetrator. Binance stated users will not bear financial costs, though some firms profited from laundering stolen assets. No evidence links Ng to the breach. The company did not comment further on the incident.

item.title: Companies Develop Kid-Safe Phones to Address Parental Concerns
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Parents want safer phones for kids. These companies are answering the call.
Companies are developing kid-safe phones to address parental concerns about unrestricted smartphone access. These devices feature modified software to restrict web browsers, social media, app stores, and other distractions. Parents can manage settings via companion apps, approving contacts, monitoring locations, setting screen time, and receiving alerts for cyberbullying or explicit content. Examples include Bark Phone, which allows gradual unlocking of features as children mature, and Gabb, which eliminates online risks by excluding social media and browsers. Pinwheel offers customizable modes for different times of day, while Teracube provides a tailored Android OS with parental controls. Ooma MyPhone and Tin Can are landline-style options with limited features. Newer entrants like Waffle and Yello! offer screen-free or restricted devices. Pricing ranges from $99.99 to $240, with monthly service plans starting at $7.99. All emphasize safety, control, and age-appropriate functionality.

item.title: Blumhouse to Adapt 'Exquisite Corpses' into Horror Franchise
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Horror Comic ‘Exquisite Corpses’ Will Kill It Up with Two Adaptations
Blumhouse Atomic acquired the horror graphic novel 'Exquisite Corpses' for a multimedia franchise. The comic, written by James Tynion IV, co-written and illustrated by Michael Walsh, and colored by Jordie Bellaire, blends elements of The Purge and Ready or Not. It features wealthy families gathering deadly killers for a Halloween-themed survival game every five years. A first-look deal between Blumhouse and Tynion’s Tiny Onion Studios includes a movie and series, with Tynion praising the studio’s commitment to horror. The first 13-issue series ended with three killers slated for spinoffs, and a sequel set in a new town is scheduled for 2027. Blumhouse CEO Jason Blun highlighted Tynion’s storytelling and their prior collaboration on 'Something Is Killing the Children,' which already has a movie and adult animated series in development. The comic debuted in 2025.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Old iPods Can Be Repurposed as Flash Drives
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Your old iPod could be a sleeper flash drive
Old iPods can be repurposed as flash drives by enabling Disk Use. Pre-iOS iPods function as USB drives on Mac and Windows, but offer less storage than modern flash drives and limited USB 2 speeds. To use as a drive, enable Disk Use via Finder on Mac or iTunes/Apple Devices on Windows. Files stored this way are invisible on the iPod itself but accessible on computers. iPods formatted for Mac use HFS+, which Windows can't read without third-party tools. Restoring the device on a Windows PC sets it to FAT32 for broader compatibility, though file size limits apply. Disk Mode, a diagnostic tool, can revive frozen iPods by toggling the Hold switch and pressing buttons. A 30-pin cable is required for connectivity. The Sprout Pi Mainboard adds modern features to select iPod models. These methods work only on iPods with a Click Wheel or 7th-gen nano, not iPod touch devices.

item.title: Bantu Expansion Transformed Africa's History and Technology
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: The Bantu expansion changed Africa. Scientists are still tracing how.
Ancient iron-smelting furnaces near Great Zimbabwe reveal advanced metallurgy. These structures, some spanning an adult's arm width, used natural-draft technology to produce iron tools without manual bellows. Archaeometallurgist Ezekiel Mtetwa notes the scale and sophistication of the furnaces. Research links these innovations to Bantu-speaking communities who migrated across eastern and southern Africa starting 6,000-4,000 years ago. Their expansion introduced farming, livestock, pottery, and metalworking to regions previously dominated by hunter-gatherers. Today, around 350 million Africans speak Bantu languages, and many carry Bantu DNA. The migration reshaped Africa's history, technology, and demographics, with genetic traces found in African Americans and Afro-Latinos as well.

item.title: Hitman Devs Craft Elusive Targets Without Scanning, Emphasize Handcrafted Detail
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Hitman World of Assassination devs say Elusive Targets are captured from studying talent over many hours and 'bespoke craftsmanship' rather than scans — 'You can have the 3d mesh completely right and still not feel like it looks like the person'
IO Interactive creates Hitman World of Assassination Elusive Targets through handcrafted design rather than scanning. Senior level designer Marin Ansdal stated no motion-capture or scanning is used, emphasizing bespoke craftsmanship. Characters are built from hand-drawn concepts, with artists balancing realism and caricature to achieve likeness. Junior artist Lovisa Österman explained spending hours studying references to capture textures and details like freckles and skin imperfections. 'You can have the 3d mesh completely right and still not feel like it looks like the person,' she said, stressing the importance of textures for recognition. The process involves meticulous study of talent to ensure accuracy beyond just 3D modeling.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Raspberry Pi 5 16GB Model Now Costs Triple Its Launch Price Amid RAM Shortage
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Raspberry Pi 5 price hike means the 16GB model now costs three times what it did at launch — and of course, the global RAM shortage is to blame
Raspberry Pi raised the 16GB Pi 5's price to $385, more than triple its $120 launch price in January 2025. CEO Eben Upton cited a lack of alternative 16GB DRAM supply and broader component shortages as the cause. The price increase is cumulative, with earlier hikes starting in December 2025, pushing the board 70% higher than launch by April 2026. Memory makers predict supply constraints will persist until 2030, with SK Hynix and Micron warning of shortages lasting into 2028 or beyond. Despite higher prices, demand for the Pi 5 grew 47% in the latest quarter. Upton advised buyers to opt for lower-density variants or older models to avoid overpaying for memory. The 8GB Pi 5 now costs $175, making the extra 8GB on the 16GB model more expensive than a standalone 8GB board. Entry-level boards like the 1GB Pi 4 and Pi 5 remain at $35 and $45, respectively. Upton warned against inflated prices from unapproved resellers and emphasized the shortage's temporary nature, though industry forecasts suggest otherwise.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Kobalt Tools Face Multiple Safety Recalls with Specific Model Alerts
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: Kobalt tools you didn't know were recalled (and what to do if you own them)
Kobalt tools have multiple safety recalls affecting various models. A July 2026 recall covers 24V and 48V trimmers, blowers, mowers, chainsaws, and pruning saws with USB-C batteries. Charging these tools while the battery is installed can cause short circuits and fires. Affected models include the 270-CFM blower (KHB 324-06) and kits with KOC 1024-06. Users should stop using these batteries and visit Greenworks' recall site. A September 2020 recall addresses 12-inch chainsaws with a faulty switch that can become permanently 'on,' risking laceration injuries. Models KCS 120-07 or KCS 120 with date codes from November 2013 to March 2020 are affected. Another September 2020 recall covers 40V pole saws that may continue running after trigger release, with model numbers 796791, 1083769, etc. A May 2017 recall targets 20-inch dual-blade mowers with circuit board fire hazards. Users should remove batteries and contact CPSC at 888-266-7096 for repairs. All affected tools require immediate action to prevent injury.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Raspberry Pi Zero 2W turned into retro terminal with CRT monitor
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: I turned a 1990s Samsung CRT into a retro terminal with a Raspberry Pi Zero 2W
A user repurposed a Samsung SyncMaster 793s CRT monitor and Raspberry Pi Zero 2W into a dedicated terminal. The setup uses a 32GB SD card with Raspberry Pi Lite OS, which lacks a GUI and uses 150MB of RAM at idle. The device boots directly to a terminal interface via SSH, allowing remote access to LAN devices. The user plans to move a self-hosted Wikipedia instance to this setup and may add retro elements like a Cool Retro Terminal emulator, a vintage keyboard, and a 3D-printed casing. The project serves as a low-cost, functional terminal for managing headless systems, with the CRT providing a nostalgic aesthetic.

item.title: U.S. Accuses Nvidia CEO of Romantic Tie to Chinese Spy Linked to Chip Smuggling
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware, TechCrunch, PCMag Original headline: U.S. Intelligence Alleges Chinese Spy Tied to Nvidia CEO's Relationship
U.S. intelligence officials claim Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had a romantic relationship with Alice Huang, a suspected Chinese spy linked to Singapore-based data center firm Megaspeed. Alice Huang, allegedly recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security, is accused of helping Chinese entities bypass U.S. export controls by smuggling Nvidia’s advanced AI chips. Huang, married for 41 years, denies the claims, calling interactions with customers routine. China dismisses the accusations as 'groundless smears.' Megaspeed, accused of smuggling $2 billion in chips to China via its subsidiary Speedmatrix, faces a Singaporean investigation, though Alice Huang is not directly targeted. Taiwan has placed her under surveillance. The U.S. House summoned Huang for a security briefing, citing intelligence reports of a 'honeypot' operation targeting him. Nvidia asserts its security protocols protect against espionage. Investigations reveal inconsistencies in Alice Huang’s career, including disputed roles at Hunan TV and CITIC Securities. The U.S. Commerce Department accuses Megaspeed of violating export controls since 2024. Chinese officials call the allegations 'unsubstantiated.'
item.source: Latest from Tom's Hardware, TechCrunch, PCMag

item.title: Amazon’s Basic Kindle Offers Affordable, Lightweight Reading Option
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Amazon’s new basic Kindle proves you don’t need all the bells and whistles
Amazon released its redesigned Kindle lineup in October, featuring a thinner, lighter 6-inch basic model starting at $169.99. The device lacks features like warm light, color display, and waterproofing but offers a 300 ppi screen, USB-C port, and 16GB or 32GB storage. It is 11% lighter and 14% thinner than the 2024 model, weighing 140g. The aluminum version costs $189.99 with 32GB storage. While premium models like the Paperwhite ($199.99) or waterproof variants offer additional features, the basic Kindle remains the most affordable option for readers prioritizing portability. Amazon claims the device is faster and more comfortable for long reading sessions, with a 6-week battery life. The basic model also includes a new flush-front screen and improved touch sensitivity to prevent accidental taps.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Why you should never put your PlayStation 5 on a carpeted floor
item.description:
Source: Engadget
Sony advises against placing PlayStation 5 consoles on carpeted floors due to dust accumulation and overheating risks. While guidelines mention avoiding long-fiber carpets, specifics for different models are unclear. The original PS5 lacks vents, while Slim and Pro models have vents requiring horizontal placement. Carpet traps bacteria, dust, and debris near vents, increasing hardware damage risks. Physical hazards like stepping on hidden objects also apply. Experts recommend solid surfaces with at least 4 inches of clearance around the console. Overheating can occur from poor placement or lack of maintenance, with third-party repairs noting issues from vertical positioning. Signs include loud fans, shutdowns, or error messages. Proper ventilation and regular cleaning are advised to prevent long-term damage.

item.title: PROFILE: Kevin Lewandowski's AeroPress and Discogs Obsessions
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: Discogs’ Kevin Lewandowski can’t live without his AeroPress
Kevin Lewandowski, founder of Discogs, discusses his reliance on the AeroPress coffee maker, which he uses multiple times daily. The platform, launched 25 years ago, serves as a comprehensive music database and marketplace for vinyl collectors, featuring forums, user-generated content, and rare record trading. Lewandowski describes his work environment as chaotic, with 30-50 browser tabs open. He avoids social media posting but engages with X and Instagram occasionally. His interests include tinkering with Home Assistant for smart home automation. He expresses a desire to create a rhythm game akin to Rez, a 2000s video game. Lewandowski emphasizes physical media, recently purchasing four records from a Portland store and three reissues from the Moodsville series. He humorously suggests a biopic tagline of 'The Secret Weapon' and shares a meme combining Discogs with a North Korean war room image, though advised against sharing it publicly.

item.title: AI Disrupts Cybersecurity, Sparks Industry Crisis
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: AI broke the cybersecurity world. What’s next?
AI is disrupting cybersecurity, triggering a wave of breaches and forcing experts to confront a new era of threats. Alex Stamos, Cognition’s chief security officer, describes the current state as a 'dark age' of cyber defense, where AI-powered tools enable adversaries to automate attacks at unprecedented scale. Recent breaches include Binance, Cursor, and Fireworks, with the latter’s stolen API keys leading to 5,000 potential breaches via a malicious plugin. Stamos highlights how AI reverses the traditional 'kill chain' by allowing real-time vulnerability detection and exploit generation, exemplified by tools like ARTEX and GLM-5.3. He compares the situation to the 1990s 'Wild West' era, noting the rise of a global, lawless ecosystem of hackers with access to powerful tools. Stamos warns that the industry is unprepared for this shift, with companies struggling to adapt as attacks become faster and more pervasive. The crisis underscores the need for urgent reforms in security practices and infrastructure to counter AI-driven threats.
